questions.text: What are the final values of Q1 and Q0 after 4 clock cycles, if initial values are 00 in the sequential circuit shown below:
questions.solution:
Both T inputs are 1. The first flip-flop toggles every clock, and Q0 clocks the second one, so the circuit is a 2-bit ripple counter (mod 4).

After 4 clock cycles it comes back to the start: Q1Q0 = 00.

Answer: 00

questions.text:
Consider the logic circuit given below:

Q=__________?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Gate 1: [latex]\overline{CD}[/latex]
- Gate 2: [latex]\overline{B\cdot\overline{CD}}[/latex]
- Gate 3: [latex]\overline{AB}[/latex]
- Output NAND: [latex]Q=B\cdot\overline{CD}+AB=AB+B(\bar C+\bar D)=AB+B\bar C+B\bar D[/latex]

Answer: [latex]AB+B\bar C+B\bar D[/latex]

questions.text: In the standard IEEE 754 single precision floating point representation, there is 1 bit for sign, 23 bits for fraction and 8 bits for exponent. What is the precision in terms of the number of decimal digits?
questions.solution:
Precision = 23 fraction bits + 1 hidden bit = 24 bits.

[latex]\log_{10}2^{24}=24\times0.301\approx7.2[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] about 7 decimal digits.

Answer: 7

questions.text:
Let [latex]\oplus[/latex] denote the Exclusive OR (XOR) operation. Let '1' and '0' denote the binary constants. Consider the following Boolean Algebra for F over two variables P and Q.
[latex]F(P,Q)=((1\oplus P)\oplus (P\oplus Q)) \oplus ((P\oplus Q) \oplus (Q\oplus 0))[/latex]
The equivalent expression for F is
questions.solution:
XOR is associative and [latex]a\oplus a=0[/latex]:

[latex]F=1\oplus P\oplus P\oplus Q\oplus P\oplus Q\oplus Q\oplus0=1\oplus P\oplus Q=\overline{P\oplus Q}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\overline{P\oplus Q}[/latex]

questions.text: The above synchronous sequential circuit built using JK flip-flops is initialized with [latex]Q_{2}Q_{1}Q_{0}[/latex] = 000. The state sequence for this circuit for the next 3 clock cycles is
questions.solution:
From the circuit: [latex]J_2=\bar Q_1, K_2=Q_0[/latex]; [latex]J_1=Q_2, K_1=\bar Q_2[/latex]; [latex]J_0=Q_1, K_0=\bar Q_0[/latex].

- 000: J2K2 = 10 (set), J1K1 = 01 (reset), J0K0 = 01 (reset) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 100
- 100: J2K2 = 10, J1K1 = 10 (set), J0K0 = 01 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 110
- 110: J2K2 = 00 (hold 1), J1K1 = 10, J0K0 = 11 (toggle) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 111

Answer: 100, 110, 111
